To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students' comprehension of Italian films, when supported with the use of a linguistic analysis of the film segments and the use of a "mental schema" as an anchoring tool, is a good starting point for the development of students' production of the language.

(a) watching films in Italian in the original version can help students in developing the ability to write Italian; (b) watching films in the original version without subtitles can be useful for students in building a "mental context" for language acquisition; and (c) the ability to write in Italian can be developed in a short amount of time (three months).

(1) watching films in the original language can contribute to the development of linguistic competence; (2) watching films in a language that is not one's own can contribute to the formation of mental images, or schemas, and mental scenarios for "anchoring" comprehension; and, (3) the comprehension of a film in the original language and the subsequent production of a text in the foreign language can be facilitated through the analysis of the language of the film.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of film segments in the teaching of Italian as a foreign language, in the context of a course for first-year university students.
how students learn to write Italian.
the role of "mental anchors" in the process of production of Italian by beginner language learners from the comprehension of spoken Italian from extracts of films in their original version.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of film segments as a teaching tool in a foreign language classroom is a very efficient way to help the students to develop a "contextual" memory bank which is essential for language comprehension and production.
the comprehension of the Italian language by means of the analysis of the segments from films has been an effective way of developing the production skills of students at the beginner level.
the use of films and the analysis of language can be a useful tool in the process of learning Italian as a foreign language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the students have acquired an ability to write and to produce a coherent and meaningful text in Italian.

we have shown that the comprehension of the language as it is used in its social context, and the use of mental images, or schemas, and mental scenarios to "anchor" the comprehension, represent the organization of our knowledge at the linguistic and cognitive, pre- and post-linguistic level, and mobilize what is available.

the use of films in the classroom can be very useful for the development of linguistic competences, as well as for the formation of cognitive skills, such as the ability to form mental images and mental scenarios that are useful to "anchor" comprehension and production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of film clips can be a very effective tool for language teaching, especially in the early stages of language learning.
students can develop writing competence after watching short clips from films in the original language.
the use of authentic audiovisual material can be used to develop a contextual memory bank, which can then be drawn upon for language production.
